reason: The only cited evidence (E1) merely states that anti-oxidation coatings are 'still required' for Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys and does not provide any data on aluminide coatings, Al2O3 formation, oxygen barrier effectiveness, or mechanical property retention for HfNbTaTiZr. None of the key premises are supported by specific prior evidence.
premises: Aluminide coatings form adherent Al2O3 scales that act as oxygen diffusion barriers on refractory alloys
Pack cementation can deposit a thin, dense aluminide coating on HfNbTaTiZr
The Al2O3 scale prevents oxygen ingress and oxidation-driven embrittlement at 1000 °C
The coating does not alter the substrate's microstructure or mechanical integrity
Coated HfNbTaTiZr retains yield strength and ductility comparable to uncoated alloy at 1000 °C
